title: Neighbourhoods
note: Outlines follow official town (chōme) boundaries, so their edges are those of the towns, not of what people call the place. Outlines marked approximate are not official districts. Small names appear as you zoom in.
credit: Town boundaries: 2020 Population Census small-area boundary data, Statistics Bureau of Japan. 出典：政府統計の総合窓口(e-Stat)（https://www.e-stat.go.jp/）「令和2年国勢調査 小地域（町丁・字等）境界データ」（総務省統計局）を加工して作成. Nine patches by the Sumida (Akihabara to Kiyosumi) © OpenStreetMap contributors.
source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries (Government of Japan Standard Terms of Use 2.0, CC BY 4.0 compatible), fetched 2026-11-18; nine patches from layers/neighbourhoods.json (OSM, ODbL). Builder: build_tokyo_neighbourhoods_layer.py
legendNote: Each neighbourhood has its own colour. Tap one to read what it is known for today and its key sites.

features.name: Akihabara
features.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundaries (ODbL), merged: 千代田区 外神田一丁目, 外神田三丁目, 外神田四丁目, 神田佐久間町一丁目, 神田花岡町, 神田相生町, 神田練塀町, 神田松永町 and 台東区 秋葉原. Approximate: Akihabara is not an official district; the blocks are those people call Akihabara. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m).
lines: Chiyoda, Taitō (千代田区・台東区)
• Akihabara Radio Kaikan (秋葉原ラジオ会館)
• Akihabara Radio Center (秋葉原ラジオセンター)
• Kanda Myōjin shrine (神田明神) (just outside the outline)
features.note: An area of electronics shops, anime and games culture, tourism and office buildings, centred on the main street Chūō-dōri near Akihabara Station. Shopping towers, parts arcades and a large camera store stand close together.

features.name: Kodemmachō
features.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundary (ODbL): 中央区 日本橋小伝馬町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m).
lines: • Ishimachi bell of time (石町時の鐘)
• Site of the Denmachō prison (伝馬町牢屋敷跡)
features.note: A mixed area of offices, small wholesalers and homes along Edo-dōri. In the Edo period it held the shogunate's main prison, and the park and memorials on that ground are the main sights.

features.name: Ningyōchō
features.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundaries (ODbL), merged: 中央区 日本橋人形町一丁目, 二丁目, 三丁目. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m).
lines: • Koami Shrine (小網神社) (just outside the outline)
features.note: An old merchants' quarter of shops, restaurants and offices, now with new apartment towers. Amazake-yokochō is a one-way shopping street of about 400 metres, and a pottery market is held on Ningyōchō-dōri each August.

features.name: Kayabachō
features.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundaries (ODbL), merged: 中央区 日本橋茅場町一丁目, 二丁目, 三丁目. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m).
lines: • Hie Shrine Nihonbashi branch (日枝神社日本橋摂社)
• Site of Takarai Kikaku's home (宝井其角住居跡)
• Site of the map office and Inō Tadataka's home (地図御用所跡)
features.note: A business district of securities firms, other offices and hotels beside the Tokyo Stock Exchange area. A branch shrine of Hie Shrine and a few historical markers stand among the office blocks.

features.name: Shinkawa
features.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundary (ODbL): 中央区 新川一丁目, 新川二丁目 Merged. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m).
lines: • Shinkawa Park and Sumida River Terrace (新川公園)
• Oiwa Inari Tamiya Shrine (於岩稲荷田宮神社)
• Echizenbori Children's Park (越前堀児童公園)
features.note: A small area of offices, apartments and houses between the Sumida, Nihonbashi and Kameshima rivers, once a centre of the sake trade. Many drink and food firms remain. A riverside walkway follows the Sumida.

features.name: Kabutochō
features.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundary (ODbL): 中央区 日本橋兜町 (admin_level 9) Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m).
lines: • Tokyo Stock Exchange (東京証券取引所)
• Birthplace-of-banking plaque, Mizuho Bank Kabutochō branch (銀行発祥の地)
features.note: Japan's stock exchange stands here. The trading floor closed in 1999 and trading is electronic. Owner Heiwa Real Estate has turned older bank buildings into restaurants, a bakery, a hotel and galleries. Few people live here.

features.name: Kakigarachō and Hakozaki
features.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundary (ODbL): 中央区 日本橋蛎殻町一丁目, 日本橋蛎殻町二丁目, 日本橋箱崎町 (箱崎町 admin_level 9) Merged. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m).
lines: • Takao Inari Shrine (高尾稲荷神社)
features.note: An area of offices, wholesalers and apartments next to Ningyōchō; Hakozaki is mostly offices under expressway viaducts. Suitengu shrine holds its monthly fair on the 5th.

features.name: Saga and Kiyosumi (Fukagawa)
features.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundary (ODbL): 江東区 佐賀一丁目, 佐賀二丁目, 清澄一丁目, 清澄二丁目, 清澄三丁目 Merged. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m).
lines: • Saga Inari Shrine (佐賀稲荷神社)
features.note: A district across the Sumida from Nihonbashi, with riverside warehouses and homes in Saga and a known café scene in Kiyosumi. Kiyosumi Garden is its best-known sight, and the two bridges carry cultural-property status.

features.name: Okachimachi
features.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundary (ODbL): 台東区 上野三丁目, 上野五丁目, 上野六丁目, 台東三丁目, 台東四丁目. Approximate: Okachimachi is not an official district; the blocks are those round JR Okachimachi station. Merged. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m).
lines: • Ameyoko market street (アメヤ横丁) (just outside the outline)
features.note: A shopping area around Okachimachi Station, between Ueno and Akihabara. Ameyoko, a market street of about 400 shops, runs along the elevated tracks. A department store, a seafood store and a discount store stand nearby.

features.name: Marunouchi and Ōtemachi
lines: • Tokyo Station Marunouchi building (東京駅丸の内駅舎)
• Mitsubishi Ichigōkan Museum (三菱一号館美術館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 千代田区 丸の内, 千代田区 大手町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The business district between Tokyo Station and the Imperial Palace. Offices, shops and museums stand in and around the restored red-brick station building, finished in 2012.

features.name: Yūrakuchō and Hibiya
lines: • Tokyo Kōtsū Kaikan (東京交通会館)
• Tokyo Midtown Hibiya (東京ミッドタウン日比谷)
• Tokyo Takarazuka Theatre (東京宝塚劇場)
• Tokyo International Forum (東京国際フォーラム) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 千代田区 有楽町, 千代田区 内幸町, 千代田区 日比谷公園. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A station area of offices, cinemas, department stores and bars along the railway viaduct, beside Hibiya Park. Hibiya Park opened in 1903 as a Western-style public park.

features.name: Kasumigaseki and Nagatachō
lines: • National Diet Library, Tokyo Main Library (国立国会図書館)
• Former Ministry of Justice building (法務省旧本館)
• Constitutional Memorial Hall, temporary site (憲政記念館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 千代田区 霞が関, 千代田区 永田町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The government district: ministries, the National Diet and the prime minister's offices. Few shops, and quiet outside office hours. Visitors come for the Diet, the Diet Library and Hie Shrine.

features.name: Kanda
lines: • mAAch ecute Kanda Manseibashi (マーチエキュート神田万世橋)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 千代田区 内神田, 千代田区 神田司町, 千代田区 神田多町, 千代田区 神田淡路町, 千代田区 神田須田町, 千代田区 神田小川町, 千代田区 神田錦町, 千代田区 神田美土代町, 千代田区 鍛冶町, 千代田区 神田鍛冶町, 千代田区 神田紺屋町, 千代田区 神田北乗物町, 千代田区 神田富山町, 千代田区 神田美倉町, 千代田区 岩本町, 千代田区 神田岩本町, 千代田区 神田東松下町, 千代田区 神田西福田町, 千代田区 神田東紺屋町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees. Area of the nine Wednesday patches removed.
features.note: A commercial area of offices, small shops and apartments between Kanda and Akihabara stations. The Kanda River runs along its north side, and a former station building from 1912 now holds shops.

features.name: Jimbōchō
lines: • Kanda used-book street (神田古書店街)
• Sanseidō Kanda-Jimbōchō main store (三省堂書店神田神保町本店)
• Jimbōchō Theatre building (神保町シアタービル)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 千代田区 神田神保町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A district of used and new bookshops along Yasukuni-dōri and nearby streets, with curry restaurants and small theatres. Sanseidō's main store reopened in March 2026 after a rebuild. A used-book festival is held every autumn.

features.name: Ochanomizu
lines: Chiyoda, Bunkyō (千代田区・文京区)
• Musical-instrument shops of Ochanomizu (お茶の水楽器店街)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 千代田区 神田駿河台, 文京区 湯島(一丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A hill by the Kanda River with universities, schools, a row of musical-instrument shops, a Russian Orthodox cathedral and a Confucian temple. Hijiri Bridge crosses the river between the two sides.

features.name: Kudan
lines: • Kudan Kaikan Terrace (九段会館テラス)
• Nippon Budōkan (日本武道館) (just outside the outline)
• Chidorigafuchi moat and greenway (千鳥ヶ淵) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 千代田区 九段北, 千代田区 九段南. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A hilltop area north of the palace moats. Yasukuni Shrine and its museum stand here, with the Shōwa-kan war-history museum and the Kudan Kaikan building. Cherry blossom time is the most crowded.

features.name: Nihonbashi
lines: • Nihombashi Mitsukoshi main store (日本橋三越本店)
• Mitsui Memorial Museum (三井記念美術館)
• Bank of Japan main building (日本銀行本店)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 中央区 日本橋, 中央区 日本橋室町, 中央区 日本橋本町, 中央区 日本橋本石町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees. Area of the nine Wednesday patches removed.
features.note: The old merchant centre of Tokyo. A road-origin marker for Japan's national roads is on Nihonbashi bridge, which sits under an expressway. Historic stores, new shopping complexes and offices stand around it.

features.name: Yaesu and Kyōbashi
lines: • Artizon Museum (アーティゾン美術館)
• Tokyo Midtown Yaesu (東京ミッドタウン八重洲)
• National Film Archive of Japan (国立映画アーカイブ)
• Yaesu Underground Mall (八重洲地下街)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 中央区 八重洲, 中央区 京橋. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: An office district east and south of Tokyo Station, with big new towers on the Yaesu side. Kyōbashi holds an art museum and a national film archive. The main Yaesu Book Center closed in 2023.

features.name: Ginza
lines: • Wakō main building and clock tower (和光)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 中央区 銀座. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A high-end shopping and entertainment district. Luxury flagships, department stores and restaurants line the streets, centred on the Chūō-dōri and Harumi-dōri crossing at Ginza 4-chome.

features.name: Tsukiji
lines: • Tsukiji Outer Market (築地場外市場)
• Namiyoke Inari Shrine (波除稲荷神社)
• Tsukiji Uogashi retail market (築地魚河岸)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 中央区 築地. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The wholesale fish market moved to Toyosu in 2018, and its former site is to be redeveloped. The outer market of shops and restaurants stays open. Tsukiji Hongan-ji, a 1934 temple, is nearby.

features.name: Tsukishima and Tsukuda
lines: • Tsukishima Monja Street (月島もんじゃストリート)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 中央区 月島, 中央区 佃. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: Reclaimed land at the mouth of the Sumida River. High-rise housing stands beside old wooden houses on back streets. Nishinaka-dōri, called Monja Street, has about 75 monja shops. Tsukuda is the origin of tsukudani.

features.name: Shimbashi and Shiodome
lines: • Old Shimbashi Station replica (旧新橋停車場)
• Nittele Giant Clock (日テレ大時計)
• Panasonic Shiodome Museum (パナソニック汐留美術館)
• Hama-rikyu Gardens (浜離宮恩賜庭園) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 新橋, 港区 東新橋. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A station area beside the Shiodome tower district. A replica of the first Shimbashi station, a museum and a shopping complex stand in Shiodome, and Hama-rikyu Gardens lies next to it.

features.name: Toranomon
lines: • Okura Museum of Art (大倉集古館)
• The Okura Tokyo hotel (ホテルオークラ東京)
• Kotohira-gu shrine (虎ノ門金刀比羅宮)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 虎ノ門, 港区 愛宕. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: An office district of tall towers. Toranomon Hills Mori Tower opened in 2014 and its Station Tower in 2023. Older places remain nearby: Atago Shrine on its small hill, and Kotohira-gu shrine beside an office building.

features.name: Roppongi
lines: • Roppongi Hills Mori Tower (六本木ヒルズ森タワー)
• The National Art Center, Tokyo (国立新美術館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 六本木. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: Roppongi Hills is built around the Mori Tower, with an art museum, a garden and a tree-lined street. The National Art Center is nearby, as are many embassies. The crossing is the centre of the bar and club image.

features.name: Azabu and Azabu-Jūban
lines: • Azabu-Juban shopping street (麻布十番商店街)
• Juban Inari shrine (十番稲荷神社)
• teamLab Borderless (チームラボボーダレス)
• Arisugawa-no-miya Memorial Park (有栖川宮記念公園)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 麻布十番, 港区 元麻布, 港区 西麻布, 港区 南麻布, 港区 東麻布, 港区 麻布台, 港区 麻布狸穴町, 港区 麻布永坂町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: Azabu-Juban is an old-fashioned area of small shops, restaurants and boutiques among apartments. Azabudai Hills, a large new complex, opened in November 2023; teamLab Borderless has been inside it since February 2024.

features.name: Akasaka
lines: • Akasaka Hikawa Shrine (赤坂氷川神社)
• Akasaka Palace State Guest House (迎賓館赤坂離宮)
• Toyokawa Inari Tokyo Betsuin (豊川稲荷東京別院)
• Tokyo Midtown (東京ミッドタウン)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 赤坂, 港区 元赤坂. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A district of offices, shops and hotels, with upscale flats, between Toranomon and Roppongi. Akasaka Sacas is a TV-company-led redevelopment beside Akasaka Station. Hikawa Shrine and Toyokawa Inari are among the older places.

features.name: Aoyama
lines: • Taro Okamoto Memorial Museum (岡本太郎記念館)
• Omotesando avenue (表参道) (just outside the outline)
• Meiji Jingu Gaien ginkgo avenue (明治神宮外苑 イチョウ並木) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 北青山, 港区 南青山. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A fashion area with flagship shops along Omotesando and Kotto-dori, and quieter streets behind. Aoyama Cemetery and the Nezu Museum garden are green spaces. The Gaien sports grounds are being redeveloped; the ginkgo avenue is to be kept.

features.name: Shiba and Hamamatsuchō
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 芝公園, 港区 芝大門, 港区 浜松町, 港区 芝. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: Offices, temples and parkland. Zojo-ji stands next to Tokyo Tower (333 m, opened 1958) in Shiba Park. Hamamatsucho, to the north, is a business and shopping area with housing mixed in.

features.name: Shirokane
lines: • Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum (東京都庭園美術館)
• Institute for Nature Study (国立科学博物館附属自然教育園)
• Meiji Gakuin Chapel and Memorial Hall (明治学院)
• Shirokane Hikawa Shrine (白金氷川神社)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 白金, 港区 白金台. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: Quiet residential streets on a plateau, with large green spaces. Shirokanedai has restaurants, cafes and boutiques. The Teien Art Museum is in a 1933 prince's residence, and the Institute for Nature Study is about 20 hectares of woodland and ponds.

features.name: Takanawa
lines: • Sengaku-ji temple and the graves of the 47 ronin (泉岳寺)
• Takanawa Okido gate ruins (高輪大木戸跡)
• Takanawa Gateway City (高輪ゲートウェイシティ) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 高輪. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A hilly area of temples and shrines, with large hotels in the south. Sengaku-ji holds the graves of the Ako retainers. Takanawa Gateway City, on the old rail depot, opened in stages from March 2025.

features.name: Odaiba
lines: Minato, Kōtō, Shinagawa (港区・江東区・品川区)
• Odaiba Seaside Park, with the Statue of Liberty replica (お台場海浜公園)
• Fuji TV headquarters (フジテレビ本社ビル)
• Miraikan, National Museum of Emerging Science (日本科学未来館)
• DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, Gundam statue (ダイバーシティ東京 プラザ)
• Decks Tokyo Beach (デックス東京ビーチ)
• Rainbow Bridge (レインボーブリッジ) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 港区 台場, 江東区 青海, 品川区 東八潮. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A reclaimed waterfront area of malls, parks, hotels and the Fuji TV building. The Palette Town ferris wheel and Venus Fort closed in 2022; Toyota Arena Tokyo opened on that site in autumn 2025.

features.name: Shinjuku
lines: • Isetan Shinjuku flagship store (伊勢丹新宿店)
• Kinokuniya Shinjuku main store (紀伊國屋書店新宿本店)
• Shinjuku Suehirotei rakugo theatre (新宿末廣亭)
• Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (新宿御苑) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 新宿区 新宿. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The east side of the station has large department stores, a rakugo theatre and a main bookshop around Shinjuku 3-chome. Hanazono Shrine and Shinjuku Gyoen garden are the quiet places among the crowds.

features.name: Nishi-Shinjuku
lines: • Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observatories (東京都庁展望室)
• Shinjuku Central Park (新宿中央公園)
• Park Hyatt Tokyo (パークハイアット東京)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 新宿区 西新宿. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: An office district of skyscrapers west of the station, with hotels and shopping near the station and older housing farther west. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building has two free observation decks, both open for sightseeing since May 2024.

features.name: Kabukichō
lines: • Kabukicho Ichibangai street (歌舞伎町一番街)
• Tokyu Kabukicho Tower (東急歌舞伎町タワー)
• Godzilla head, Shinjuku Toho Building (新宿東宝ビル)
• Golden Gai (新宿ゴールデン街)
• Cinecity Square (歌舞伎町シネシティ広場)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 新宿区 歌舞伎町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A large entertainment district of bars, clubs and love hotels, busy late into the night. Tokyu Kabukicho Tower opened in April 2023. Young people gathering near the Toho building has been a concern since 2019.

features.name: Shin-Ōkubo
lines: • Kainaka Inari Shrine (皆中稲荷神社)
• Korea Town east of the station (コリア・タウン)
• Hyakunincho ethnic restaurants west of the station (百人町)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 新宿区 百人町(一,二丁目), 新宿区 大久保(一,二丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: Around the station, the east side is a Korean town of cosmetics shops, restaurants and K-pop goods. The west side, in Hyakunincho, has restaurants and food shops from across Asia and Muslim-majority countries. Many young people visit.

features.name: Kagurazaka
lines: • Kagurazaka slope and main street (神楽坂)
• Akagi Shrine (赤城神社) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 新宿区 神楽坂, 新宿区 袋町, 新宿区 若宮町, 新宿区 岩戸町, 新宿区 横寺町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A slope with side alleys of restaurants, traditional inns and cafes. It was once a geisha district. Akagi Shrine was rebuilt in 2009 to 2010 with a condominium on part of its land.

features.name: Takadanobaba
lines: • JR Takadanobaba Station and its Astro Boy departure melody (高田馬場駅)
• Used bookshops on Waseda-dori west of the station (早稲田通り)
• Anahachiman Shrine (穴八幡宮) (just outside the outline)
• Mizu-Inari Shrine and Takada Fuji (水稲荷神社) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 新宿区 高田馬場. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A major student area with many universities, cram schools and low-priced restaurants, and a large Myanmar community. The JR platforms play the Astro Boy theme as a departure melody. Used bookshops line Waseda-dori west of the station.

features.name: Yotsuya
lines: • Tokyo Toy Museum (東京おもちゃ美術館)
• Suga Shrine (須賀神社) (just outside the outline)
• Sainen-ji temple, grave of Hattori Hanzo (西念寺) (just outside the outline)
• Arakicho and Tsunokami Benzaiten (荒木町) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 新宿区 四谷. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A mixed office and housing area along Shinjuku-dori near Yotsuya Station, once the edge of Edo's outer moat. Small museums, shrines and temples are within a short walk; Arakicho to the south keeps a Showa-era feel.

features.name: Hongō and Yayoi
lines: • University of Tokyo Hongo campus (東京大学本郷キャンパス)
• University Museum (東京大学総合研究博物館)
• Yayoi Museum and Yumeji Takehisa Museum (弥生美術館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 文京区 本郷, 文京区 弥生. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: An academic area with publishers, hospitals and housing, where Natsume Soseki and Higuchi Ichiyo once lived. The University of Tokyo's Hongo campus, on the former Kaga domain residence, covers parts of Hongo and Yayoi.

features.name: Yushima
lines: • Yushima Seido (湯島聖堂) (just outside the outline)
• Former Iwasaki residence garden (旧岩崎邸庭園) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 文京区 湯島(二,三,四丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A small town of offices and commerce in 2-chome, high-end housing in 4-chome and medical firms in 1-chome. Yushima Tenman-gu holds a plum festival from early February to early March, with about 200 white plum trees.

features.name: Nezu and Sendagi
lines: • Mori Ogai Memorial Museum (文京区立森鷗外記念館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 文京区 根津, 文京区 千駄木. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A low-rise historic area on the north-east edge of Bunkyo, where renovated shops and cafes have made it a walking destination. Nezu Shrine has seven Important Cultural Property structures and an azalea festival in April and May.

features.name: Kōrakuen
lines: • Koishikawa Korakuen garden (小石川後楽園)
• Tokyo Dome City Attractions (東京ドームシティ アトラクションズ)
• LaQua and Spa LaQua (ラクーア)
• Baseball Hall of Fame Museum (野球殿堂博物館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 文京区 後楽, 文京区 春日(一丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: Tokyo Dome City has the baseball dome, amusement rides, a spa complex and a boxing and wrestling hall. Next door is Koishikawa Korakuen, an Edo-period garden begun in 1629; its main foliage season is November.

features.name: Komagome
lines: • Toyo Bunko Museum (東洋文庫ミュージアム)
• Komagome Fuji Shrine (駒込富士神社)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 文京区 本駒込, 豊島区 駒込. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A quiet residential area inside the Yamanote line with old temples, shrines and green space. Rikugien, built by 1702, has evening lighting in late November and early December. The Toyo Bunko museum reopened in January 2026.

features.name: Ueno
lines: • Tokyo National Museum (東京国立博物館)
• National Museum of Western Art (国立西洋美術館)
• Ameyoko shopping street (アメ横) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 台東区 上野公園, 台東区 上野(一,二,四,七丁目), 台東区 池之端, 台東区 東上野(三,四丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees. Area of the nine Wednesday patches removed.
features.note: A 53-hectare public park, Japan's first (1873), holds museums, the zoo, Shinobazu Pond and a shrine. The zoo's giant panda exhibit ended in January 2026. Ameyoko, about 400 shops, runs along the tracks.

features.name: Yanaka
lines: • Yanaka Ginza shopping street (谷中銀座)
• Asakura Museum of Sculpture (朝倉彫塑館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 台東区 谷中, 台東区 上野桜木. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: An old temple and cemetery district north of Ueno. Its sloping shopping street has about 60 shops and eateries, and the lanes around it are low-rise and local. Yanaka Cemetery holds the grave of the last Tokugawa shogun.

features.name: Asakusa
lines: • Hanayashiki amusement park (浅草花やしき)
• Kappabashi kitchenware street (かっぱ橋道具街)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 台東区 浅草, 台東区 雷門, 台東区 花川戸, 台東区 西浅草. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The temple quarter around Sensō-ji, entered through the Kaminarimon gate and the Nakamise approach street of about 90 shops. Behind the main street are Asakusa Shrine, the Hanayashiki amusement park and the kitchenware wholesale street of Kappabashi.

features.name: Kuramae
lines: • Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine (第六天榊神社)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 台東区 蔵前. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A district on the west bank of the Sumida River, once the site of the Edo rice granaries. Today it mixes offices and homes, with toy wholesalers along Edo-dōri and a few shrines and temples.

features.name: Ryōgoku
lines: • Ryōgoku Kokugikan sumo hall (両国国技館)
• Honjo Matsuzaka-chō Park, Kira mansion site (本所松坂町公園)
• Sumida Hokusai Museum (すみだ北斎美術館) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 墨田区 両国, 墨田区 横網. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The home of the Kokugikan sumo hall, which holds tournaments in January and September. The Edo-Tokyo Museum reopened here on 31 March 2026 after four years closed. Temples, a garden and memorial sites are within a short walk.

features.name: Oshiage (Skytree)
lines: • Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー)
• Tokyo Solamachi shopping complex (東京ソラマチ)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 墨田区 押上, 墨田区 業平. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The district around Tokyo Skytree, 634 m tall, and the Solamachi shopping complex of about 312 stores at its base. The Sumida Aquarium is inside the same complex. A few old temples and shrines stand in the streets behind it.

features.name: Mukōjima
lines: • Mukōjima-Hyakkaen Garden (向島百花園) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 墨田区 向島. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A residential riverside area on the east bank of the Sumida with old shrines and temples, a long park along the embankment and Hyakkaen, a flower garden founded around 1804.

features.name: Kinshichō
lines: • Sumida Triphony Hall (すみだトリフォニーホール)
• Chigusa Inari Shrine (千種稲荷神社)
• Tokyo Rakutenchi building with Kinshichō PARCO and cinema (東京楽天地)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 墨田区 錦糸, 墨田区 江東橋. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The commercial centre of the Sumida east side, with large store buildings, cinemas and a concert hall around the station. North of the line is a park with a shrine in its corner.

features.name: Monzen-Nakachō and Fukagawa
lines: • Fukagawa Nakachō shopping street (深川仲町通り商店街)
• Fukagawa Tokyo Modern-kan (深川東京モダン館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 江東区 門前仲町, 江東区 富岡, 江東区 深川, 江東区 冬木, 江東区 福住. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees. Area of the nine Wednesday patches removed.
features.note: An old temple and shrine district in Fukagawa. Tomioka Hachiman Shrine holds a festival in mid-August, and Fukagawa Fudōdō, a branch of the Narita temple, holds fire rituals daily. A shopping street runs between them.

features.name: Shirakawa and Miyoshi
lines: • Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (東京都現代美術館)
• Fukagawa Edo Museum (深川江戸資料館)
• Kiyosumi Garden (清澄庭園) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 江東区 白河, 江東区 三好, 江東区 平野. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees. Area of the nine Wednesday patches removed.
features.note: A quiet part of Fukagawa with the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo, the Fukagawa Edo Museum and the large Kiba Park nearby. Kiyosumi Garden, a Tokyo-designated scenic garden, lies just beyond the outline.

features.name: Kameido
lines: • Funabashiya kuzumochi main shop (船橋屋 本店)
• Kameido Katori Shrine (亀戸香取神社)
• Kameido Sengen Shrine (亀戸浅間神社)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 江東区 亀戸. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The area around Kameido Tenjin, a shrine known for wisteria in late April and early May and plum blossom in February and March. Funabashiya, a kuzumochi sweet shop dating from 1805, stands on the approach street.

features.name: Toyosu
lines: • Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai (豊洲 千客万来)
• teamLab Planets (チームラボプラネッツ)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 江東区 豊洲. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A reclaimed waterfront district. The fish market, moved from Tsukiji in 2018, has public viewing walkways. Nearby are the Senkyaku Banrai food and hot-spring complex (opened February 2024), teamLab Planets (scheduled to run to late 2027) and a mall.

features.name: Shinagawa-shuku
lines: • Old Tōkaidō road, Kitashinagawa Honchō-dōri (旧東海道・北品川本通り)
• Shinagawa Shrine (品川神社) (just outside the outline)
• Tōkai-ji temple (東海寺) (just outside the outline)
• Shinagawa-ji temple (品川寺) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 品川区 北品川(一,二丁目), 品川区 南品川(一,二丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: The first post town on the old Tōkaidō road out of Edo. The old road, now Kitashinagawa Honchō-dōri, still has small shops, and shrines and temples stand along or just off it.

features.name: Togoshi-Ginza
lines: • Togoshi Ginza shopping street (戸越銀座商店街)
• Togoshi Hachiman Shrine (戸越八幡神社)
• Togoshi Park (戸越公園) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 品川区 戸越(一,二丁目), 品川区 平塚(二,三丁目), 品川区 豊町(一丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A residential area built along a shopping street about 1.3 km long with about 400 shops. Locals shop here daily.

features.name: Naka-Meguro
lines: • Naka-Meguro Hachiman Shrine (中目黒八幡神社)
• Naka-Meguro Kōkashita, shops under the railway arches (中目黒高架下)
• Starbucks Reserve Roastery Tokyo (スターバックス リザーブ ロースタリー 東京) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 目黒区 上目黒(一,二,三丁目), 目黒区 中目黒(一,二,三丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A district beside the Meguro River, which has cherry trees along its banks in Meguro Ward. Shops sit under the railway arches near the station, and a few shrines and temples stand a short walk away.

features.name: Jiyūgaoka
lines: • Kuhonbutsu River Greenway (九品仏川緑道)
• Marie Claire Street (マリクレール通り)
• Kuhonbutsu Jōshin-ji temple (九品仏浄真寺) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 目黒区 自由が丘. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: An upscale residential and shopping district with many pastry shops and a European-style streetscape. Narrow roads make it busy on foot. A covered stream is now a green walkway.

features.name: Den-en-chōfu
lines: • Den-en-chōfu Station building, replica (田園調布駅)
• Ginkgo avenues west of the station (西口の放射状道路)
• Kikkōyama Kofun burial mound (亀甲山古墳)
• Tamagawa Sengen Shrine (多摩川浅間神社)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 大田区 田園調布, 大田区 田園調布本町, 大田区 田園調布南. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A planned residential suburb with roads radiating from the station and lined with ginkgo trees. The station building is a replica rebuilt in 2000. Near the river are a park with ancient burial mounds and a Fuji shrine.

features.name: Shibuya
lines: • Shibuya Scramble Crossing (渋谷スクランブル交差点)
• Shibuya Sky observation deck (渋谷スカイ)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 渋谷区 渋谷(一,二,三丁目), 渋谷区 道玄坂, 渋谷区 宇田川町, 渋谷区 神南. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A shopping and entertainment area around the station. Very large crowds use the scramble crossing in front of the station. New towers such as Shibuya Sky stand beside older shopping streets like Center-gai.

features.name: Harajuku and Omotesandō
lines: • Ōta Memorial Museum of Art (太田記念美術館)
• Meiji Jingu (明治神宮) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 渋谷区 神宮前. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A youth fashion street, Takeshita-dōri (about 350 m), and the Omotesandō approach road with large shops, set beside the large forest of Meiji Jingu. Togo Shrine and a small ukiyo-e museum are in the back streets.

features.name: Ebisu
lines: • Yebisu Garden Place (恵比寿ガーデンプレイス)
• Yebisu Brewery Tokyo (ヱビス ブルワリー トウキョウ)
• Tokyo Photographic Art Museum (東京都写真美術館) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 渋谷区 恵比寿, 渋谷区 恵比寿南, 渋谷区 恵比寿西. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A station area built around Yebisu Garden Place, on the site of a former beer brewery. The Yebisu Brewery Tokyo visitor facility opened there on 3 April 2024, and a photography museum is in the same complex.

features.name: Daikan-yama
lines: • Hillside Terrace (ヒルサイドテラス)
• Daikanyama T-Site bookstore (代官山蔦屋書店)
• LOG ROAD DAIKANYAMA (ログロード代官山)
• Sarugaku-zuka mound and Sarugaku Shrine (猿楽塚・猿楽神社)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 渋谷区 代官山町, 渋谷区 猿楽町, 渋谷区 鉢山町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A hillside residential area with a low-rise shopping and gallery complex, Hillside Terrace (built in phases from 1969 to 1998), a bookstore complex and a historic house. Boutiques, bakeries and cafes line its streets.

features.name: Hiroo
lines: • Arisugawa-no-miya Memorial Park (有栖川宮記念公園) (just outside the outline)
• Tokyo Metropolitan Central Library (東京都立中央図書館) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 渋谷区 広尾. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A quiet residential area with a shopping street, a large Rinzai temple and, just over the boundary in Minami-Azabu, a hillside park with the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Library.

features.name: Shimokitazawa
lines: • Shimokitazawa shopping streets (下北沢一番街など)
• Shimokita Ekiue (シモキタエキウエ)
• Kitazawa Hachiman Shrine (北沢八幡神社) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 世田谷区 北沢(二,三丁目), 世田谷区 代沢(五丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A low-rise district with small theatres, live music venues, vintage shops and narrow lanes. Newer buildings have been added along the old Odakyu line route, such as Mikan Shimokita, opened in 2022, and reload.

features.name: Sangenjaya
lines: • Carrot Tower (キャロットタワー), top-floor observation space on the 26th floor
• Setagaya Public Theatre (世田谷パブリックシアター)
• Echo Nakamise shopping street (エコー仲見世商店街)
• Taishido Hachiman Shrine (太子堂八幡神社) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 世田谷区 三軒茶屋, 世田谷区 太子堂(二,四丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A commercial and residential district in Setagaya. A covered shopping lane and the Suzuran street are in front of the station. The Carrot Tower complex stands in the next town, Taishido.

features.name: Futako-Tamagawa
lines: • Futako-Tamagawa Park and Kishin-en garden (二子玉川公園・帰真園)
• Futako Bridge (二子橋), 1925 road bridge over the Tama River
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 世田谷区 玉川(一,二,三,四丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A riverside district beside the Tama River. East of the station, the Futako-Tamagawa Rise complex was finished in 2015 and sits next to a large park. The river bank and a riverside park lie a short walk away.

features.name: Seijō
lines: • Seijo 3-chome Green Space (成城三丁目緑地)
• Toho Studios (東宝スタジオ), seen from outside only
• Kashio Toshio Inventions Museum (樫尾俊雄発明記念館), free by advance reservation
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 世田谷区 成城. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: An upscale residential district and school town centred on Seijo Gakuen, where many entertainment figures live. Streets are quiet, with small gardens and green spaces. Toho's film studio stands in the north-east near the station.

features.name: Gōtokuji
lines: • Gotokuji temple (豪徳寺), including the beckoning-cat hall
• Graves of the Ii family at Gotokuji, a national historic site
• Setagaya Castle Site Park (世田谷城阯公園)
• Gotokuji shopping street (豪徳寺商店街)
• Setagaya Hachimangu shrine (世田谷八幡宮) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 世田谷区 豪徳寺. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A calm residential area in Setagaya. Gotokuji temple, with its offered beckoning cats and the graves of the Ii family, is the main reason to come. The remains of Setagaya Castle lie close by.

features.name: Nakano
lines: • Nakano Broadway (中野ブロードウェイ), home of the Mandarake head office
• Nakano Sunmall shopping arcade (中野サンモール)
• Nakano Shikinomori Park (中野四季の森公園)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 中野区 中野. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A dense west Tokyo hub with a long covered shopping street leading to Nakano Broadway, known for manga and collectors' shops. The Nakano Sunplaza hall has been closed since July 2023 and has no confirmed reopening date.

features.name: Kōenji
lines: • Koenji Hikawa Shrine and the weather shrine (高円寺氷川神社)
• Shukuhozan Koenji temple (宿鳳山高円寺), which gave the area its name
• Za-Koenji, Suginami Arts Center (座・高円寺)
• Koenji Ginza shopping street, nicknamed Junjo (純情商店街)
• Koenji Pal shopping street (高円寺パル商店街)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 杉並区 高円寺南, 杉並区 高円寺北. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A district west of Shinjuku where many young people live alone. Shopping streets around the station sell second-hand clothes and cheap food, and small live music houses are common. The Tokyo Koenji Awa Odori dance is held in late August.

features.name: Asagaya
lines: • Asagaya Pearl Center covered shopping street (阿佐谷パールセンター)
• Asagaya Shinmei-gu shrine (阿佐ヶ谷神明宮)
• Laputa Asagaya cinema (ラピュタ阿佐ヶ谷)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 杉並区 阿佐谷南, 杉並区 阿佐谷北. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A district split by the Chuo Line station into north and south sides. The Pearl Center covered street runs south from the station and hosts the August Tanabata festival. There are old bookshops, jazz cafes and live houses.

features.name: Ogikubo
lines: • Tekigaiso, former Konoe Fumimaro villa (荻外荘)
• Kadokawa Garden and Genginsanbo (角川庭園)
• Ogikubo Hakusan Shrine (荻窪白山神社)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 杉並区 荻窪, 杉並区 上荻. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A western Tokyo station town with many ramen shops. Within a short walk are two small public gardens, a restored former villa and a shrine known for cat statues. Visitor numbers are lower than in central Tokyo.

features.name: Ikebukuro
lines: • Sunshine City (サンシャインシティ), with the aquarium, observatory and Ancient Orient Museum
• Tokyo Metropolitan Theatre (東京芸術劇場), reopened September 2025
• Ikebukuro West Gate Park, nicknamed Global Ring (池袋西口公園)
• Jiyu Gakuen Myonichikan (自由学園明日館)
• Seibu Ikebukuro main store (西武池袋本店)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 豊島区 池袋, 豊島区 東池袋, 豊島区 西池袋, 豊島区 南池袋. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A major rail hub with large shops on both sides of the station. The east side has Sunshine City and anime shops; the west side has theatres and parks. The Seibu store now sits in a building owned by Yodobashi.

features.name: Sugamo
lines: • Sugamo Jizo-dori Shopping Street (巣鴨地蔵通り商店街)
• Kogan-ji temple, known as Togenuki Jizo (高岩寺)
• Shinsho-ji temple, with a bronze Jizo of 1714 (真性寺)
• Jigen-ji temple (慈眼寺), graves of Akutagawa and Tanizaki
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 豊島区 巣鴨. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: An area known for the Jizo-dori shopping street, which leads to Kogan-ji temple. The street is popular with older visitors, and the temple is busiest on days of the month containing a 4. Several temples stand nearby.

features.name: Mejiro
lines: • Gakushuin University, Mejiro campus (学習院大学)
• Postage Stamp Museum (切手の博物館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 豊島区 目白. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A quiet residential area in Toshima Ward around Gakushuin, a school with links to the Imperial family. Visitors are few. It suits walks through the streets, a small stamp museum and a Japanese garden.

features.name: Ōji
lines: • Kita City Asukayama Museum (北区飛鳥山博物館)
• Oji Shrine (王子神社) (just outside the outline)
• Otonashi Shinsui Park (音無親水公園) (just outside the outline)
• Oji Inari Shrine (王子稲荷神社) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 北区 王子. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A district in northern Tokyo with a cherry-tree hill park holding three museums. Oji Shrine gave the area its name. A fox procession to Oji Inari Shrine is held on New Year's Eve, and a stream park lies nearby.

features.name: Akabane
lines: • Akabane Ichibangai shopping street (赤羽一番街商店街)
• Akabane Suzuran-dori shopping street (赤羽スズラン通り商店街)
• Joshoji temple on the Inetsuke Castle site (静勝寺)
• Akabane Hachiman Shrine (赤羽八幡神社) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 北区 赤羽, 北区 赤羽南, 北区 赤羽西(一丁目). Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A rail junction town in northern Tokyo with busy shopping streets at the east exit and many cheap bars. Redevelopment of the west exit has reduced the older nightlife. A small temple on castle ruins stands west of the station.

features.name: Nippori
lines: • Kyoo-ji temple, with bullet holes in its gate (経王寺)
• Nippori Textile Town (日暮里繊維街)
• Yanaka Ginza shopping street (谷中銀座) (just outside the outline)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 荒川区 西日暮里, 荒川区 東日暮里. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: An old downtown area with a temple district on its west side and a fabric wholesale district east of the station. The Yanaka shopping street begins just beyond the ward line. Narrow lanes and old temples suit slow walks.

features.name: Kita-Senju
lines: • Yoshida Ema-ya, votive plaque shop (吉田絵馬屋)
• Adachi Market, fish market (足立市場)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 足立区 千住曙町, 足立区 千住旭町, 足立区 千住東, 足立区 千住大川町, 足立区 千住河原町, 足立区 千住寿町, 足立区 千住桜木, 足立区 千住関屋町, 足立区 千住龍田町, 足立区 千住橋戸町, 足立区 千住宮元町, 足立区 千住緑町, 足立区 千住元町, 足立区 千住柳町, 足立区 千住中居町, 足立区 千住仲町, 足立区 千住. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A large rail hub in Adachi with stores at the station and an old post town on the Nikko road nearby. Senju also has many public bathhouses. A fish market and an old bridge lie close to the Sumida River.

features.name: Shibamata
lines: • Katsushika Shibamata Tora-san Museum (葛飾柴又寅さん記念館)
• Yagiri no Watashi ferry, Shibamata landing (矢切の渡し)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 葛飾区 柴又. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A temple town on the Edo River, the setting of the Tora-san films. A shop-lined approach leads to Taishakuten temple. Nearby are the Tora-san museum, an old house with a garden and a small ferry across the river.

features.name: Kameari
lines: • Kochikame statues near Kameari Station (こち亀銅像)
• Kameari Katori Shrine (亀有香取神社)
• Kameari Ginza shopping street, Yuroad (亀有銀座商店街)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 葛飾区 亀有. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A station town in Katsushika once full of factories, now with shopping centres and narrow shopping streets. Statues of characters from the manga Kochikame stand near the station. Mostly visited by fans and locals.

features.name: Kichijōji
lines: • Inokashira Benzaiten hall in the park (井の頭弁財天) (just outside the outline)
• Musashino City Kichijoji Art Museum (武蔵野市立吉祥寺美術館)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 武蔵野市 吉祥寺本町, 武蔵野市 吉祥寺南町, 武蔵野市 御殿山. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A popular west Tokyo town beside Inokashira Park. Shopping arcades, a narrow lane of small bars and restaurants, and the park pond are all within walking distance.

features.name: Jindaiji
lines: • Fudo no Taki waterfall in the temple grounds (不動の滝)
• Jindai Botanical Garden (神代植物公園), closed Mondays
• Jindaiji Castle ruins in the Water Plant Garden (深大寺城跡)
features.source: e-Stat 2020 census small-area boundaries, union of: 調布市 深大寺元町, 調布市 深大寺北町, 調布市 深大寺東町, 調布市 深大寺南町. Simplified: Douglas-Peucker, tolerance 0.00003 degrees.
features.note: A quiet temple area in Chofu. Jindaiji is one of the oldest temples in Tokyo and holds a national treasure bronze statue. Soba noodles made with spring water are the local dish, and a botanical garden borders the temple.
